ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, UBOs, officers, and authorized signatories against the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List (SEMA), the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the OFAC SDN List, and the European Union consolidated sanctions list for any EU-facing commercial activity. Politically Exposed Persons are classified per FATF and PCMLTFA definitions; enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification, and senior-management approval are required for any PEP, high-risk jurisdiction, or any wealth sourced through foreign trust or shell structures. Beneficial ownership must be traced through every intermediate legal entity until natural persons are disclosed at 25% ownership or de facto direct or indirect control, in accordance with BC BCA s. 51.91(2) and the federal Corporations Beneficial Ownership Regulations.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Corporate Online, BC Corporate Registry, operated by the Province of British Columbia (https://www.bcregistry.gov.bc.ca), used together with the NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) system for Canada-wide name comparison
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A BC corporate name must be composed of letters of the Latin alphabet (English or French); a French-language version may be appended. Non-Latin scripts, including Chinese characters, must be transliterated into Latin characters. The name must be distinctive rather than merely descriptive, must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing corporate, partnership, or trademark name as determined by the NUANS phonetic and linguistic comparison, and must not mislead as to the corporate form, jurisdiction, or nature of business. A numbered company name (BC numbered corporation) may be adopted without a name reservation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may: (i) file a fresh Name Reservation Request with revised distinctive elements (statutory fee approximately CAD 30); (ii) submit a formal request for reconsideration to the Registrar of Companies of British Columbia, annexing the prior NUANS report and written legal argument demonstrating that the proposed name is distinguishable and not misdescriptive; (iii) if administrative reconsideration is unsuccessful, apply for judicial review in the Supreme Court of British Columbia. A concurrent trademark clearance search in the Canadian Intellectual Property Office database is strongly recommended before any re-filing to reduce downstream trademark infringement exposure.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for a low-risk software development company. The Business Corporations Act requires a registered office and a records office at a physical geographic address within British Columbia capable of accepting service of process during normal business hours; a P.O. Box or bare mail-forwarding address is prohibited. A virtual office operated by a licensed BC corporate services provider or law firm at an actual BC location is legally acceptable. For App Store merchant onboarding (Apple IAP and Google Play Billing), a demonstrable operating address and commercial substance are strongly preferred by payment processors; a pure virtual-mailbox address risks merchant-account rejection and adverse tax-residency characterization.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low. Quantified annual probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection is approximately 2% to 5% for a non-regulated, low-risk software application developer with no financial-services license, no significant cash handling, and no land holdings. Registry and CRA verification is ordinarily documentary only; a physical inspection would most plausibly occur only upon a CRA income-tax audit, a contracted transaction audit, or an investigative trigger referred by FINTRAC or law enforcement.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (British Columbia), SBC 2002, c. 57, s. 10 (incorporation), s. 24 (corporate names), s. 100 (share provisions), s. 182 (registered office), Part 8 (directors), s. 184 (officers)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: BC Registries and Online Services, Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Application comprising Incorporation Agreement, Notice of Articles (Form 1) and Articles (Form 2), filed through BC Corporate Online
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum issued or paid-up capital is required under the BCBCA; the Company may incorporate with nil paid-up capital. No escrow account rule is imposed. Founders' shares may be issued at CAD 0.01 per share on subscription and contributed to the corporate bank account.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: 1. That the Incorporation Agreement, Notice of Articles and Articles, as filed with the BC Corporate Registry, be ratified and adopted. 2. That the Company issue one hundred common shares at CAD 0.01 per share to the founding shareholder, and the President record the allotment and issue share certificates. 3. That the registered office and records office be established at the address stated in the Notice of Articles, and all necessary filings under the Business Corporations Act be executed. 4. That [Name] be appointed President, [Name] Secretary, and [Name] Chief Financial Officer, serving at the pleasure of the Board. 5. That Directors approve corporate bank account opening and authorize all operational documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services – Corporate Online Portal (corporateonline.gov.bc.ca)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search using the BC Registry's Name Request service; submit up to three (3) proposed corporate names in order of priority with a distinct clause, avoiding prohibited or restricted terms under s. 24 BCBCA. Upon approval the name is reserved for 56 days; the reservation number must be entered into the subsequent incorporation application.
required_dossiers: Name Request form completed through BC Corporate Online
Name search report or distinctness justification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused on distinctiveness grounds, refile with alternate names or rely on a professional NUANS report; alternatively, incorporate under a numeric designation (e.g., 1234567 B.C. Ltd.) and later file a Name Change under s. 23 BCBCA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Charter Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Corporate Registry via the incorporator or an authorized BC-based service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Incorporation Agreement, Notice of Articles (Form 1), and Articles, including any special rights and restrictions attaching to share classes. The incorporator executes the Incorporation Agreement and consents to act as first director if named. The registered office and records office addresses must be located in British Columbia. No federal articles are required because the entity is provincially incorporated.
required_dossiers: Incorporation Agreement executed by the incorporator
Consent to Act as First Director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Registry requisitions are cured by amending the draft in Corporate Online and resubmitting; statutory corrections requested before issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation do not attract an additional filing fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Application and Payment of Statutory Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services – Corporate Online (Electronic Filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into BC Corporate Online, complete the incorporation application, upload executed charter documents, enter the name reservation number, and pay the CAD 350 incorporation filing fee plus registration levy by credit card. The system issues an electronic acknowledgment; the Certificate of Incorporation is issued electronically upon completion of statutory review.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing fails validation, correct the flagged data fields and resubmit the same transaction. If the application is rejected, file a fresh application and request a refund of any duplicate fee through the registry's corporate account.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organization of the First Board of Directors Meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company Board of Directors and corporate records office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Summon the first board meeting after issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation. The board ratifies the charter, approves the subscription and issuance of shares, adopts the securities register, fixes the registered and records office, appoints officers, opens the corporate bank account, and resolves any elective filing matters. Minutes are signed and retained in the registered records office.
required_dossiers: Written minutes of the first board meeting (waiver of notice)
Share certificate book and securities register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an appointed director or officer cannot assume office, the board fills the vacancy by ordinary resolution in accordance with Part 8 BCBCA; a Director Change Form is filed with the BC Registry to update the public record.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Fiscal Registration with the Canada Revenue Agency
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency – Business Registration Online (BRO)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for the CRA Business Number (BN) and the Income Tax program, a GST/HST account (required once worldwide taxable supplies, including App Store sales, exceed CAD 30,000), and a Payroll Deductible account if employees are engaged. Maintain BC Registry director and office records, and register with WorkSafeBC when the first worker is hired.
required_dossiers: Corporate bank account details for GST/HST refunds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA rejects the BN application, reconcile the legal name and address with the BC Registry record and resubmit; contact the CRA Business Window at 1-800-959-5525 for a manual resolution.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — the enterprise is an app developer and software publisher with no manufacturing, warehousing, or physical production facility. For any leased office premises, the relevant authority is the municipal business licensing department (e.g., City of Vancouver or City of Langley).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required for mobile utility software operations; the Company maintains provincial registration and a municipal business licence only if it occupies a physical office in British Columbia.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: British Columbia Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy (Environmental Assessment Office and Environmental Management Act oversight)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — software development and IT support services (NAICS 511210) are not reviewable under the Reviewable Projects Regulation, BC Environmental Assessment Act; no EIA report, project notification, or registration certificate is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial effluent or air emissions are generated. Office wastewater discharges must comply with municipal sewer use by-laws; tenant improvements must meet low-VOC limits under the BC Consumer Products Regulation; e-waste and batteries must be diverted through approved RecycleBC product stewardship streams. No environmental permit is required for app-store-only operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For the registered office, obtain a municipal fire safety and occupancy clearance from the local fire authority and building department. Upon first hire, register as an employer with WorkSafeBC and comply with the Workers Compensation Act, OHS Regulation: workplace inspection, first-aid risk assessment, ergonomics program, and hazard communication. No civil defense or emergency preparedness permit applies to a non-industrial office occupier.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada — My Business Account portal (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html); for British Columbia provincial sales tax, the Competent Provincial Authority is the BC Ministry of Finance – Consumer Taxation Branch, eTaxBC (https://etax.gov.bc.ca)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity carrying on business or making taxable supplies in Canada must obtain a 9-digit Business Number (BN) from CRA, which serves as the TIN for income tax and GST/HST. Procedure: (1) determine whether the non-resident entity is carrying on business in Canada or exploiting a Canadian tax presence; (2) submit Form RC1 'Request for a Business Number (BN)' via CRA's Non-Resident Registration Application, or by fax/telephone under CRA International Tax Services Office protocols; (3) CRA issues BN and GST/HST account program (RT), payroll (RP), and corporation tax (RC) accounts as applicable; (4) for BC PST, register separately through eTaxBC and obtain a PST vendor registration number; (5) foreign corporations must also register extraprovincially under the BC Companies Act before or upon carrying on business in BC. No separate TIN is issued; the BN is the operative tax identifier.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or free-choice entity classification mechanism exists under Canadian tax law. Canadian business corporations are automatic separate taxpayers. Available statutory elections affecting corporate tax include Income Tax Act section 85 corporate rollover elections, section 86 reorganizations, section 93 and 95 foreign affiliate elections, section 216 non-resident rental income elections, and GST/HST Quick Method election for smaller registrants. Hybrid mismatch rules are addressed through ITA ss.18.4–18.5 and arm's-length principles; no direct hybrid entity classification election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) / Provincial Sales Tax (PST) — British Columbia applies federal GST 5% plus provincial PST 7%; no Harmonized Sales Tax in BC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: GST/HST: CAD 30,000 in annual worldwide taxable supplies (small supplier threshold) before mandatory registration with CRA. BC PST: If the vendor makes taxable retail sales to BC consumers or is deemed to have a vendor nexus in BC, registration is required; BC has no general small-supplier turnover exemption under the PST Act for retail sellers, though occasional/casual sales may be exempt if not a regular vendor.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no government-mandated real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or continuous tax audit system. GST/HST registrants with taxable supplies above CAD 1.0 million must file electronically via CRA's GST/HST e-services API; all registrants may file through a third-party software, My Business Account, or standardized EDI. BC PST returns must be filed electronically via eTaxBC. E-invoicing is voluntary under the Pan-Canadian Peppol PINT/Peppol BIS 3.0 standard; no CRA pre-approval or digital signature stamp is required for commercial invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A zero-rated export under ETA Schedule VI applies to: (i) physical goods exported from Canada pursuant to a supply; and (ii) supplies of intangibles or services made to a non-resident where the supply is not acquired for use in Canada and, for services, the service is not substantially performed in Canada. For a mobile utility app sold through Apple IAP/Google Play Billing to users outside Canada, the supply is zero-rated provided the customer is a non-resident, the digital download/access is delivered electronically to an international outlet, and the seller retains credible evidence of non-resident status. Supplies to Canadian residents, including any app-store sales transmitter denominated to Canadian users, are subject to 5% GST plus 7% PST if not specifically zero-rated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Form B13; only for tangible goods — not applicable to pure digital downloads)
Bill of Lading / Proof of Export (shipping proofs; app-store export logs with IP location and account-origin data)
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank proof of receipt of foreign currency or payout from Apple App Store Connect/Google Play Console)
Non-resident status evidence (customer records, declaration of non-Canadian address, geolocation data)
App Store financial reports and payout statements showing the split of proceeds and commissions
Export/service contract and invoice showing supply to non-resident and foreign currency settlement
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA generally has a 4-year statutory reassessment window; in cases of misrepresentation or fraud, reassessment may extend indefinitely. For fraudulent export zero-rating or failure to substantiate the non-resident nature of digital app sales, CRA may reverse the zero-rating and assess GST/HST plus interest. Penalties include ETA s.280(1) penalty of 50% of the tax improperly recovered or claimed; ETA s.285 criminal liability with fines up to 200% of the tax sought to evade or imprisonment; and BC PST assessment under the Provincial Sales Tax Act with interest and a 25% penalty for false statements / tax evasion. In particular, CRA verifies whether app-store recipients are actually Canadian consumers by analyzing payment origination, IP addresses, device carrier country codes, and app-store account territories; inadequate documentation produces clawback of refunds and loss of export zero-rating.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada). Canada operates a free-floating currency regime; there is no specialized foreign-exchange control administration. Ancillary oversight is exercised by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for deposit-taking institutions and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) for anti-money-laundering supervision.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility on both current and capital account. The Canadian dollar trades freely worldwide, and there are no exchange-control restrictions under the Currency Act or the Bank of Canada Act on the purchase, sale, conversion, or repatriation of funds. Profit remittance and dividend distributions to non-resident shareholders are unrestricted but are generally subject to Canadian non-resident withholding tax of 25%, reducible to 5%-15% under an applicable income tax treaty. The Investment Canada Act may require a new-business notification where a non-Canadian establishes a new Canadian business above the prescribed financial threshold; no exchange-control approval is required for capital inflows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender window, mandatory conversion ratio, or designated-account requirement. Exporters may retain proceeds in foreign currency in Canadian bank accounts, convert at any time at market rates, and make cross-border disbursements without central-bank approval.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium-High. Canada does not issue an 'Electronic Money Institution' (EMI) licence. Cross-border digital payment platforms (e.g., Wise, Payoneer) operate as FINTRAC-registered Money Services Businesses (MSBs) or through partnership arrangements with Schedule I banks; payment service providers subject to the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) must be registered with the Bank of Canada, with supervision effective November 2024. A British Columbia corporation may lawfully use offshore digital payment platforms for low-value cross-border payouts, but the primary operational treasury account and capital-receipt account should remain with a Canadian Schedule I bank to preserve a clean documentary trail, avoid unnecessary FX margin, and meet CRA substantiation requirements. Legal constraints include limitations on operating a foreign-currency float without an MSB registration and the need to maintain each foreign affiliate as a reporting entity under T1134/T1135 filings where applicable.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical in-branch appearance is not statutorily mandated for directors or signatories of a British Columbia corporation. For Canadian-resident principals, remote onboarding with video verification and two-factor government-issued identity verification is accepted by most Schedule I banks (RBC, TD, BMO, CIBC, Scotiabank). Non-resident directors and beneficial owners are subject to enhanced due diligence under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA); in practice, banks typically require either an in-person meeting at a Canadian branch, or a notarized and apostilled certified true copy package containing identification, proof of address, and source-of-funds declarations, plus a current corporate registry extract confirming the director and registered office. The PCMLTFA beneficial-ownership rule requires identification of every individual holding 25% or more of the corporation's shares.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Mobile utility app revenue derived predominantly from Apple App Store and Google Play billing, with no conventional paper invoices or direct merchant settlement evidence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide App Store Connect and Google Play Console payout statements, platform merchant agreements, monthly remittance advices from Apple (Ireland) and Google (Singapore), a written revenue-recognition policy aligned with IFRS 15, and sample bank statements showing platform payouts reconciled to the corporate ledger.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Non-Canadian beneficial owner or sole director controlling the BC operating company, raising source-of-funds and shell-company concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Assemble certified passport and proof-of-address for every 25% beneficial owner, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds narratives with supporting banking statements, a current BC registry extract, an organizational chart showing the full ownership chain, and notarized/apostilled identity documents where remote onboarding is requested.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Freemium business model with minimal or zero near-term revenue, no audited financial statements, and reliance on future capital injections.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a board-approved business plan, 24-month cash-flow projections, shareholder subscription agreements evidencing paid-up capital, parent-company bank statements for the originating funds, and a legal opinion confirming that no statutory license is required for the app's device-optimization scope under ISIC 6201 / NAICS 511210.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: High-frequency inbound SWIFT credits from foreign app-store intermediaries or a foreign parent without a clear intercompany narrative.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply intercompany agreements, an IFRS/TP-compliant master file, app-store platform contracts, evidence of T1134 foreign-affiliate disclosure filing, and a treasury policy specifying purpose codes such as 'Software Royalties' or 'Share Subscription' for all expected flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Trust structures, nominee shareholdings, or offshore intermediate vehicles in the ownership chain obscuring beneficial identity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver the registered trust deed, watertight beneficial-ownership register, a Canadian tax opinion confirming economic ownership, the corporate minute book with share transfers, and individual source-of-funds declarations from each ultimate principal.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Financing round settled through non-bank instruments, convertible notes, or crypto-adjacent rails, creating opacity of capital entry.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Produce subscription agreements, SAFE or convertible-note instruments, investor KYC/onboarding records from a registered securities dealer, blockchain transaction attestations where applicable, and CRA-aligned books demonstrating that the funds were converted into equity at arm's-length terms.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity from a foreign parent or non-resident investor should be transmitted by SWIFT MT103 denominated in CAD or USD to the BC corporation's operational account at a Schedule I bank and settled through Lynx, Canada's high-value payment system operated by Payments Canada. Use a precise wire reference and narrative, e.g., Field 72: '/REC/ EQUITY CONTRIBUTION - SHARE SUBSCRIPTION', and match the wire to the corporate share register. A non-Canadian investor establishing a new Canadian business must file an Investment Canada Act new-business notification within 30 days when above the threshold, and Statistics Canada may require reporting of cross-border fund transfers and direct-investment positions through its international transactions surveys. Equity injection is preferred over shareholder debt to avoid thin-capitalization limitations under subsection 18(4) of the Income Tax Act and withholding-tax leakage on interest. Third-party digital FX corridors should not be used for equity injections; only regulated Schedule I bank channels should execute the capital wire to preserve the documentary audit chain.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements should use SWIFT MT103 messages executed through a Schedule I bank over Lynx for high-value CAD/USD vendor payments, and MT101/MT103 sequences for cross-border royalty or licensing disbursements with purpose narrative 'Software Royalty / License Fee'. Commercial import and export letters of credit are issued via SWIFT MT700/MT707 through CIBC, Scotiabank, BMO, or RBC, with CAD clearing for domestic batch items through the Automated Clearing Settlement Service (ACSS) and instant retail credits through Canada's Real-Time Rail (launched 2025) where speed is required. App-store royalty remittances to Apple (Ireland) and Google (Singapore) should be executed as MT103 transactions supported by the platform agreements and a transfer-pricing policy ensuring that no Canadian withholding tax obligation is triggered on outbound software-license royalties beyond treaty-applicable rates, and that appropriate T1134/T106 disclosures are maintained.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD FX Forwards — standard tenors up to 12 months executed under ISDA/CEMA documentation with Schedule I dealing banks; non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are generally unavailable and unnecessary for CAD because of full onshore convertibility and a liquid deliverable market.
FX Swaps — spot-forward and swap combinations for managing near-term US-dollar liquidity from app-store payouts and vendor concentrations.
Cross-Currency Swaps (CAD vs USD) — including cross-currency interest rate swaps for medium-term balance-sheet hedging of foreign-parent intercompany balances.
Vanilla European-Style CAD/USD FX Options — purchased call or put options from Schedule I banks to cap conversion cost without mandatory execution, subject to board-approved derivatives policy.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BC Annual Report under the Business Corporations Act (British Columbia)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Registrar of Companies / BC Registries, Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two months after each filing-date anniversary (the anniversary of incorporation, amalgamation, or continuation).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Immediate arrears status; if a company fails to file two consecutive annual reports, the Registrar may strike it off after notice and dissolve it; property of the struck-off company vests in the Crown; directors and officers continue to face personal liability for unsatisfied corporate obligations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal T2 return including British Columbia applicable schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the corporation's taxation year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of the unpaid balance due plus 1% per month of arrears (maximum 12 months); refusal to file may result in CRA demand, further penalties, interest, and prosecution; prolonged failure does not strike the corporation but can expose directors to director-liability certificates.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: The BC Business Corporations Act does not mandate an audit based solely on revenue, assets, employees, or shareholder count for a non-reporting private BC corporation. An independent audit is compulsory when the company is a reporting issuer, when a court or the Registrar has ordered it, when shareholders have validly requisitioned an audit, or when a shareholders agreement, lender, or prescribed condition requires audited financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS is required for reporting issuers/publicly accountable enterprises; Canadian ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) is applicable for a non-reporting private BC corporation; IFRS remains an acceptable alternative for private enterprises. Financial statements should be prepared consistently under the selected framework and accompanied by directors' approval.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At each annual return cycle, review all share transfers completed in the preceding year and update the transparency/significant-control register on a timely basis (generally within 15 business days of any change). Record each individual with significant control (ISC) at 25% or more ownership or voting control, or de facto control, including the date, nature, and cessation of control. A BC provincial corporation must keep the register at its registered office and produce it on lawful demand; if the entity is an extraprovincial/federal corporation in BC, include the equivalent ISC information in the annual return filed with Corporations Canada.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Transparency Register / Register of Individuals with Significant Control

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% combined general rate (federal 15% + British Columbia 12%); 11% combined CCPC small-business rate on qualifying active business income up to CAD 500,000; 15% federal rate alone.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal SR&ED investment tax credits (35% refundable for CCPCs on first CAD 3,000,000 of eligible labour/expenditures; 15% non-refundable for other corporations) and BC Interactive Digital Media Tax Credit (17.5% refundable on eligible B.C. labour costs for qualifying mobile utility app products); BC small-business deduction yields the 2% provincial rate on first CAD 500,000 active business income.
